title: Sauerbraten
subtitle: German marinated braised beef
excerpt: Sauerbraten is one of Germany's great centrepiece dishes: a large piece of beef soaked for several days in a spiced vinegar marinade, then braised slowly until deeply tender. The marinade is not a shortcut step; it is the defining part of the recipe.
sourceNotes: Sauerbraten is one of Germany's national dishes: a large cut of beef marinated in vinegar and spices for several days before slow braising. The long marinade is not optional; it is what makes the dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze sliced sauerbraten with its sauce for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the beef for 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator before cooking. The longer the marinade, the deeper the flavour.

content.text: Sauerbraten translates roughly as 'sour roast', and the sourness comes from a long bath in spiced vinegar. The marinade both flavours and tenderises the meat: after 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator, the beef takes on a deep, complex tang that no amount of additional seasoning during cooking can replicate. Plan the start date before anything else.

The braising liquid is thickened at the end with a butter-and-flour mixture to give a sauce with body. Some regional versions stir in crushed gingernuts or raisins at this stage for a sweet-sour finish; this recipe keeps to the plainer style, but both are authentic. Serve with red cabbage and potato dumplings or mashed potato.

items.prepNote: tied into a neat shape if needed

content.text: Day 1, make the marinade: combine the red wine vinegar with 500ml of cold water in a large non-reactive bowl or zip-lock bag. Add the onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, cloves, allspice, cinnamon and sugar. Stir to dissolve the sugar, then submerge the beef. Cover and refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, turning the meat once a day.
Cooking day: lift the beef out of the marinade and pat it thoroughly dry with kitchen paper. Strain the marinade through a sieve, reserving both the liquid and the vegetables separately.

Season the beef generously with salt. Heat a large saucepan over a high heat with a splash of oil and sear the beef on all sides until deeply browned, about 8 to 10 minutes in total. Remove the beef and set aside.

Add the reserved vegetables to the pan and cook over a medium heat for 5 minutes until softened. Return the beef to the pan and pour in the reserved marinade liquid. It should come roughly halfway up the meat; top up with water if needed. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Cover the pan and cook over a very low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours, turning the beef every 45 minutes, until the meat is completely tender when pierced with a skewer. If the pan is not oven-safe, transfer to a roasting tin, cover tightly with foil, and cook in an oven set to 160C / 140C fan.

Lift the beef out and rest it under foil for 10 minutes. Strain the braising liquid into a clean pan and discard the vegetables. Bring the liquid to a simmer. In a small bowl, mash the butter and flour together with a fork until you have a smooth paste. Whisk this paste into the simmering liquid a little at a time until the sauce reaches your preferred consistency. Taste and adjust salt.
Slice the beef across the grain and arrange on a warm serving plate. Spoon the sauce over and serve the rest alongside.

items.symptom: The beef is tough after 3 hours
items.cause: The heat was too high, tightening the muscle fibres, or the cut was not a true braising cut.
items.fix: Keep the liquid at the faintest simmer: a few bubbles breaking the surface, not a rolling boil. Give it another 30 to 45 minutes and check again.

items.cause: The braising liquid has a high proportion of marinade vinegar.
items.fix: Stir a teaspoon of sugar into the finished sauce and simmer for another minute. A splash of water can also dilute acidity without altering the flavour profile significantly.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery
items.cause: Not enough butter-flour paste was added, or the sauce was not simmered long enough after thickening.
items.fix: Make a little more paste and whisk it in, then simmer for at least 5 minutes after the last addition so the flour cooks out.

items.symptom: The beef has no sour depth after cooking
items.cause: The marinade time was shorter than 3 days.
items.fix: There is no fix at the cooking stage. For next time, commit to a minimum of 3 days in the refrigerator.
